description: The left side lists the array, indices, and memory addresses. In the grid on the right, five consecutive green cells in the second row show the space allocated to the array. The other cells, in light gray, show available space.

frames.explanation: Each element in this example occupies 4 bytes, so adjacent elements have starting addresses exactly 4 apart. Leading zeros align the addresses to the same width and do not indicate octal notation.
frames.title: Array elements, indices, and addresses

result: The index gives an element's position in the array, the value is the data stored there, and the memory address identifies the start of its storage.
summary: An array uses indices starting at 0 to locate its elements. The elements occupy consecutive, equally sized regions of memory.
